'''Jonathan Darby Lubin''' (born August 10, 1936, in [[Staten Island, New York]]) is a professor emeritus of mathematics at [[Brown University]].  He received an  A.B. from [[Columbia College, Columbia University|Columbia College]] in 1957 and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] from [[Harvard University]] in 1963 under the direction of [[John Tate (mathematician)|John Tate]]. He taught at [[Bowdoin College]] from 1962–1967 and at Brown University from 1967–2000.

He and Tate introduced [[Lubin–Tate formal group law]]s and used them to construct explicit local [[class field theory]].
